The story follows a clear and logical progression where every element serves the central theme of disillusionment and the limits of superficial charm. The beginning establishes Q's "frictionless" persona in college, specifically highlighting how he effortlessly ended a relationship with a girl named Clara and how the narrator wondered how Q would handle "velvet-gloved ruthlessness" like firing someone. This directly sets up the middle of the story, where the narrator witnesses Q ten years later attempting to use those exact same tactics to fire a competent employee named Meredith. When Meredith refuses to be charmed and exposes Q's incompetence, the illusion is shattered. This leads logically to the satisfying conclusion, where the narrator feels a sense of relief upon realizing that Q is subject to the same "gravity" and real-world friction as everyone else.
